### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via TranslationBundle (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via TranslationBundle (symbol, a top-level type))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c0033f9d7e9ee49404db6390a7953eb4bb5152e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7f5bc4b022981672cd39cdd784677422ddc6491e` — the merge of head `1e112d65fd7552e0d844732a20c2db77bbd93404` into base `3c0033f9d7e9ee49404db6390a7953eb4bb5152e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7f5bc4b022981672cd39cdd784677422ddc6491e && git checkout 7f5bc4b022981672cd39cdd784677422ddc6491e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3c0033f9d7e9ee49404db6390a7953eb4bb5152e 1e112d65fd7552e0d844732a20c2db77bbd93404 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3c0033f9d7e9ee49404db6390a7953eb4bb5152e && git merge --no-ff 1e112d65fd7552e0d844732a20c2db77bbd93404

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c0033f9d7e9ee49404db6390a7953eb4bb5152e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3c0033f9d7e9ee49404db6390a7953eb4bb5152e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `274a4bd5bffdcec618998245f7b2ae4b09653728`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-field-label-duplicate-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/lint-duplicate-field-labels.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-duplicate-field-labels.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.unknown-picklist-binding-refusal.test.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/system/translations/index.ts, examples/app-todo/src/translations/zh-CN.ts, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx, content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx, content/docs/ui/react-pages.mdx, .changeset/33545-duplicate-field-labels.md (narrowing face: every path of the diff). Read, not reviewed: `translateObject`, `builtinSystemFieldLabel`, `localeChain`, `resolveLocaleAmong` and `BUILTIN_SYSTEM_FIELD_LABEL_LOCALES` in packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts; packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts; packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts, system-fields.ts and runtime-gate.ts; packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts and protocol-authoring-channel.ts; packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (injection order, packaged base); packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`translateOptionsFor`); the three generated platform bundles named in ③.

Inputs read: card #33545 body and all four comments (triage 6886885827, claim 6887573651, amendments 6887617666 and 6887847864, dev report 6888745802); parent #33506 body and all comments; PR #33639 body, its 16-file list and the net diff against `origin/main`. Check-runs on the head as read: 50 runs, none failed. Completed green: Check Changeset (one of two), Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Auto Label, filter. Still running: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, the second Check Changeset, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, two scoped lints, Live E2E UI, Plan Test UI shards, Test Core 1 to 8 of 8, all four Type Check lanes. ⛔ This verdict is on the design; the derived gate families (tests, type check, repo gates) had not answered when it was written, and `in_progress` is not a pass. The seat reads them green before any landing step.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, CLI: an object with two or more non-hidden, labelled fields that share a trimmed label, as authored or in any compared locale, now fails `os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` (and the consumers of the same registry: `os verify`'s author-time step, scaffold validation). Right: it is the card's item 1 and the claim's severity line.
- Accept set, publish door: `runtimeTypes: ['object']`, so an `object` write with `state: 'active'` and the draft to active promotion are judged. Right for the ruling as written. `object_extension` writes are not judged by this rule (see ④, finding 1).
- Not narrowed: load. Read in the tree: system columns are injected at registration, no boot or registration path calls the registry of author-time rules, the control-plane install channel (`package-author`) and the `migrate-stored` pass return before the rules. "Installed apps unaffected at load" is right.
- Public surface: `@objectstack/lint` gains `lintDuplicateFieldLabels`, `FIELD_LABEL_DUPLICATE`, `DuplicateFieldLabelFinding` and one `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entry. Additive. Right.
- `@objectstack/spec`: one semantic registry entry, no schema, no export, no conversion. Right: no lossless mechanical move exists (which field keeps the label is not recorded), so a TODO-only entry is the correct ADR-0087 shape.
- Shipped metadata: three zh-CN field labels relabelled in two examples, plus one action-param label, one comment and one report label and description that name the same idea. The last three are not fields the rule judges; they keep the bundle's wording coherent and are inside "shipped example metadata". Accepted.
- Docs: four transcripts move 67 to 68. Consistent with one added registry entry; the drift gate that pins it was still running.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves. The changeset bumps `@objectstack/lint` minor (the rule, the exports) and `@objectstack/spec` minor (the registry entry). Both correct. No other released package's source moves: the metadata-protocol hunks are test fixtures, the examples and docs publish nothing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body, the title carries `!`, the body carries the BREAKING banner, three FROM to TO lines each with its one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered object-field-label-duplicate-refused`) that matches the entry's `id`. The upgrade prescription an author hit by it reads is complete: rename, `hidden: true`, or drop the duplicate and use the platform column, and the bundle-only case says to translate apart in that bundle. No tracker number in any runtime string or in the changeset. Level and declaration: correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions`: empty. No deviation declared. File surface: every path is inside claim 6887573651 as widened by 6887617666 (four transcripts, count only: confirmed, one line each) and 6887847864 (fixtures, relabel only: confirmed below).
- Card item 2 (error or warning for installed objects): recorded in the claim and repeated in the changeset, the rule's module note, the explanation and the registry entry. Answered.
- Card item 1 names "the one the AI builder's integrity check calls". The dev states that check lives in cloud and nothing was done there. From this repository that cannot be confirmed either way. What the tree does show is that every REST, Studio and MCP `object` publish passes the door. Escalated as a note for the seat: say on the card whether the cloud integrity check reaches this door or needs its own wiring.
- Out-of-scope finding (three platform objects clash only in generated bundles): confirmed in the tree at this head, in `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/`. `ru.objects.generated.ts`: `sys_import_job.created_count` and `sys_import_job.created_at` carry the same label (lines 3580 and 3633). `ar.objects.generated.ts`: `sys_oauth_resource.id` and `sys_oauth_resource.identifier` carry the same label. `fr.objects.generated.ts`: `sys_user.accountable_user_id` and `sys_user.manager_id` are both "Responsable" (lines 100 and 111). None of the six fields is `hidden` in its object source. It is not this PR's to fix: no author door judges platform objects, and the PR does not make these worse. It does need a card, not only a note: it is a reproducible reader-facing defect (Prime Directive 10), the dev left it "noted, not filed". File it unassigned as a finding for triage to route, p3; the fix is three translated-locale string edits in the platform-objects bundles (hand-written values, `pnpm check:i18n` gates them), which is platform-objects i18n work and not the lint lane's.

### ④ Design judgment

Narrowing against the published spec on `main`: the spec declares a field `label` as free text with no uniqueness, and `main` builds an object with two same-label visible fields. The narrowing takes that away at the author door and at the publish door, on purpose and by the card. It does not make a consumer tolerate anything; it is a refusal at the producer, which is the Prime Directive 12 direction.

The `hits` file, `18.object-field-label-duplicate-refused.ts`, sentence by sentence against the code: `surface` names the three places a label comes from and the code reads exactly those (`objects[].fields`, `objectExtensions[].fields` through `objectsAsServed`, `translations[]` per locale). `replacement` names the three fixes the hint prints. "the metadata publish door (422 on an object write)" matches `runtimeTypes: ['object']`. `acceptanceCriteria` says a stored object in the shape is still served and its next save through the door is refused: matches the gate (below). The entry carries no `relevance`, so it lists for every stack in `os migrate meta`; allowed (the field is optional) and honest. Holds.

Attempts to break it, each read in the cited code:

- Visibility. "Visible" is the static `hidden: true` only, on the field as served. Injected `organization_id`, `owning_business_unit_id` and `queue` are `hidden: true` in the spec's own tables; `owner_id` and the four audit columns are not, so those five are compared, as the text says. A column the object does not carry is not compared: the rule takes the injected set from `injectedSystemColumnDefs`, the plan the registry itself injects from (`ownership: 'none'`, `systemFields: false`, tenancy off), and the `ownership: 'none'` case is pinned. An authored field under an injected name replaces the injected definition, as at registration. No false positive found on that axis. A field left out of one view is still compared: the rule is object-level and the default surfaces still draw both, which is the ruling.
- Locales. One authored pass, then one pass per locale: every key of the stack's bundles plus the four built-in system-label locales, through `translateObject`. Checked against `builtinSystemFieldLabel`: the read exit translates an injected column whose label still equals its English default by matching the request locale against that table with no bundle at all, so the built-in passes are real reader behaviour and are what catches the parent card's case. Checked against the registry: system columns are injected before the contributor definition is stored, so the packaged base carries `owner_id` under its English default and the built-in label applies to packaged objects too; the examples' relabels are therefore true positives, not artefacts. A locale with no translation for a field keeps the authored label in the rule and at the read exit alike. A bundle-only clash names its locale (pinned).
- Door differential. `addedFindings` in `runtime-gate.ts` subtracts the baseline (the universe without the written item) and, from the stored universe, only findings located on ANOTHER entry. The rule's path is `objects[i].fields` on the written entry, so: a write that creates the clash is refused; a sibling write is not charged (its finding is in the baseline); a re-save of an object that already carries the clash is refused. That last behaviour is the gate's documented rule for every gating rule ("a finding located on the written item itself is this write's ... Re-saving a row is writing it"), identical for the roll-up and autonumber rules on the same door, and it is stated in the changeset, the explanation, the module note and the registry entry. It does lock every edit of that one object, an unrelated field included, until the clash is fixed; the fix is available in the same save (relabel or hide) and the refusal names both fields and the three fixes. Other objects, reads, load, the `migrate-stored` pass and the control-plane install channel are untouched. Honest and consistent.
- Fixtures. `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`: four `label: 'Owner'` to `'Owner Name'` on a `text` field named `owner`; `protocol.unknown-picklist-binding-refusal.test.ts`: the helper's `'Tier'` to a per-field label. No assertion, expectation or test name changes in either file; no assertion in either file reads a label; the remaining literal `'Tier'` at line 248 is an `object_extension` body the rule does not judge. Neither file holds a deliberate duplicate-label case. Relabel only.
- New tests. Nine rule cases and three door cases cover the parent card's pair, both controls (hidden, relabelled), `ownership: 'none'`, bundle-only clash, authored clash, authored `owner_id`, registry wiring on three commands, sibling write, re-save and heal. The explanation test pins the named locales to the spec table, so the prose cannot drift from it.

Findings:

1. should-fix (a follow-up card discharges it; fixed on this head it earns a delta review). `object_extension` is a gated door type for other rules, and this rule declares `['object']` only. An extension write that adds a second field under an existing label is published unjudged, which reproduces the parent card's defect through the other object-shaped door. The stored extension is then folded onto its target in the snapshot (`objectsAsServed` reads `objectExtensions`), so the target's next `object` save is charged with a clash the extension created. The PR's text is accurate about its own reach ("an `object` write"), so nothing shipped is false; the gap is coverage. Card for `domain:spec`: judge `object_extension` writes with this rule (the `18.object-extension-door-*` entries are the precedent for doing that as its own change).
2. nit. The rule calls `translateObject` with the locale alone. The read exit also passes the deployment's `fallbackChain` and `defaultLocale` (`translateOptionsFor`), both readable from `stack.i18n`. The two agree unless a fallback-locale bundle gives a field a label different from its authored one and the field has no entry in the read locale; then the rule can report a clash a reader with that fallback does not see, or miss one. "Through the same `translateObject` the `/meta` read serves them with" is true of the function, not of its options. Follow-up card or accepted deviation; not a correctness risk for the ruled case.
3. nit. At the door the snapshot carries no translations (the PR says so). Stated consequence: a bundle-only clash is not caught there. Unstated mirror: an authored label that equals a built-in system label in one of the four locales is refused at the door even when the deployment's own bundle translates it apart in that locale, while `os build` over the same stack passes. Rare (it needs an authored label in one language and a bundle for the same language). One sentence in the explanation would cover it.
4. nit (prose). `visibleWhen` is not consulted, and neither is `group`: two fields with complementary `visibleWhen`, or the same label under two field groups (a billing and a shipping "City"), are refused. That is inside the ruling (grid headers, export and import columns ignore both), and the sweep found no such case in the examples, the first-party apps or HotCRM, but it is the most likely way an author meets this rule outside the owner case, and neither the changeset nor `os explain` names it. Add one sentence on a prose face, or leave it.
5. nit. A field with no `label` is not compared, on the premise that it is drawn under its unique name. If a surface derives a display label from the name, an unlabelled `owner` beside `owner_id` is a clash the rule cannot see. Miss only, never a false finding.
6. nit. Two fields that clash as authored and are both translated to one other label in a bundle produce two findings for one defect (the group key includes the label). Cosmetic.

No must-fix. No false positive on legitimate metadata was found on the visibility, system-field or locale axes beyond the corners graded above.

## ACCEPT · PR #33639 (#33545) · head `1e112d65fd7552e0d844732a20c2db77bbd93404` (base sync of reviewed head `274a4bd5`) · 2026-11-15T05:28Z

## 席位核对

- **形态:** 16 files, +525/−15 (read from the PR's file list): new author-time rule `lintDuplicateFieldLabels` (`FIELD_LABEL_DUPLICATE`, error) in `packages/lint`, wired into the authoring-rule registry with `runtimeTypes: ['object']`, its explanation and nine rule cases plus three door cases; one semantic registry entry `object-field-label-duplicate-refused` in `packages/spec`; three zh-CN relabels in two examples; relabel-only fixtures in two `metadata-protocol` tests; four docs transcripts 67 → 68; a minor changeset for `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec` with the BREAKING banner and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 33639`: 0 of 16 paths, 540 lines): Tier S.

- **门禁 check-runs:** on this head 68 runs: 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed (`Test UI` 16 of 16 shards green on this run). `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **契约复审:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on the reviewed head `274a4bd5`, record 6888857868; this head adds only the two base syncs (no must-fix, one should-fix, five nits). Ruling-ref for the in-seat review: 「你有 fable ，车道契约复审可以自己做」.
- **接受的偏差:** should-fix 1 (an `object_extension` write is not judged by this rule) is discharged by card #33644 (p3, `domain:spec`, `Blocked-by: #33639`); the PR's own text says "an `object` write", so nothing shipped is false. Nits 2 to 6 (fallback-chain options, the door's no-translation mirror case, `visibleWhen`/`group` not consulted, unlabelled fields not compared, doubled findings) are accepted as they stand; none is a false refusal of the ruled case.
- **范围外去向:** three platform objects clash only in generated bundles (`sys_import_job` ru, `sys_oauth_resource` ar, `sys_user` fr) → card #33645 filed as a finding, triaged p3 `domain:spec` and now in flight on this seat. Card item 1's "AI builder integrity check" lives in the cloud repo, which this seat cannot read: every REST, Studio and MCP `object` publish in this repo passes the door, and whether the cloud check reaches it stays open for the cloud lane.
- **落地条款:** ready + auto-merge now under the maintainer's standing order 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」 (2026-10-25T11:35Z) and 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-07T16:59Z). K read on the synced head after its rerun: K = 13 commits on `main` past PRBASE `3c0033f9` (the Test Core affected-set diff base of this run; < 15, no new language pack since). The reviewed head `274a4bd5` had K = 21 when its CI went green, so the seat merged `main` in by the relay base sync (no conflict; the PR's own net diff is unchanged, the merge brings in only `main`'s own edits to three of its paths: `cli.mdx`, `validating-metadata.mdx` and `rule-explanations.ts`) and reread the gates.
